title: Harmonize interactive surface and shadow system for dense layouts
creator: Ava Morgan
description: Align color tokens, spacing/radius scales, and elevation shadows specifically for dense UI surfaces (tables, compact lists, toolbar components). Aim is to produce a small, coherent set of surface tokens and shadow presets that improve contrast, reduce visual noise in high-density views, and preserve accessibility for text and interactive controls.
background: Context: Previous token updates focused on global scale and compact typography, but we lack clear guidance and presets for densely packed surfaces (compact tables, mini toolbars, dense list-views) where current elevation and radii feel visually inconsistent across components. Multiple engineering and product tickets have surfaced visual churn when switching between compact and default density. This work will create a minimal surface/elevation system and a density-aware application guide for components.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 surface color tokens for dense surfaces (surface-dense-1/2/3) with clear WCAG AA contrast against body text at compact sizes
Provide 3 shadow/elevation presets tuned for dense contexts (dense-elev-0/1/2) with visual parity across Chrome/Firefox/macOS
Publish a spacing/radius scale variant for dense mode (radius-dense-1/2) and map to existing components (button, table-row, chip)
Update component tokens and provide migration guide and code examples for buttons, tables, and compact cards
Design QA checklist and automated visual regression test vectors for dense mode across major breakpoints
design_notes: Decision: Use subtle elevation steps with reduced blur and offset (smaller Y, smaller blur) to avoid 'floating' appearance in dense lists
Decision: Surface colors will be semantic (surface-dense) rather than purely numeric to make usage intent clearer for engineers
Tradeoff: Increased contrast on dense surfaces may reduce perceived depth; we'll balance with stronger separators on table rows where needed
Accessibility: Verified with simulated text sizes down to 12px and medium weight; token candidates must meet AA contrast against text color
Implementation note: Provide both CSS custom properties and JSON token bundle for runtime theming; include a densify() utility in the token library to switch scales
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with Engineering (J. Kim) and Product (R. Singh). Agreed scope: tokens + component mapping + migration guidance.
2026-03-04: Exploratory Figma frames created (dense table, compact toolbar, miniature chip). Initial shadow presets applied and reviewed internally.
2026-03-08: Contrast checks run for 6 candidate surface colors; 3 shortlisted. Shared with Accessibility for feedback.
2026-03-10: Engineering provided perf feedback: prefer token count < 20 for dense mode to keep bundle size low. Adjusted proposals.
2026-03-12: First implementation PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/482). Linking Figma refs in PR. Requesting design review from Lina and Mateo.
technical_considerations: Ensure shadow presets translate to box-shadow values that perform well on Chrome (avoid heavy spread radius)
Provide tokens in raw (rgba) and compressed (hex + alpha) forms for server-side rendering pipelines
Consider adding utility mixins for dense-border-separator to reduce token proliferation across table implementations
implementation_plan: Finalize token palette and elevation presets in Figma (design)
Export token JSON and add densify() variant to token library (engineering)
Update components: button, table-row, chip, toolbar to reference dense tokens behind a density flag
Ship migration guide and small code samples for frontend teams; coordinate with SDK owners for React/Vanilla kits
Monitor visual regression dashboard for 2 weeks post-release and roll back if regressions exceed threshold
qa_steps: Visual: Compare before/after snapshots for compact table at 320px, 768px, 1440px
Accessibility: Run Axe on dense component pages with text-size 12px and ensure no contrast violations
Cross-browser: Validate shadows on Chrome, Firefox, Safari on macOS/Windows
Regression: Run screenshot diff suite and confirm < 0.8% pixel diff for stable components
